source.title: Scaling, Simplification, and Adaptation: Lessons from Pretraining on Machine-Translated Text
source.authors: Dan John Velasco; M. T. Roque

record.tranche_reason: Measures held-out language-model cross-entropy across model sizes, as scaling studies do, but in the new setting of pretraining on machine-translated data and evaluating on native text.
record.gate_note: The study reports scaling results for held-out native-text loss in Figure 1 and §5.1. Its downstream-task and syntactic-probe results are not recorded here: they do not test whether downstream performance is predictably related to pretraining loss or scale. It does not fit power laws or test extrapolation or compute-optimal allocations.
record.test_reason: Trains GPT-2 models at 124M, 355M and 774M on machine-translated corpora and reports held-out native-text cross-entropy by size (Fig. 1, §5.1). It also reports fine-tuned downstream and syntactic-probe accuracy by size (Tables 5, 6, 8, 9). This is a new setting (MT-derived pretraining, native evaluation) for the claim. The test is weak: three sizes spanning under one order of magnitude, no power-law fit, and a fixed token budget per condition. T3 fits better than T1 because no power-law fit is made and the data setting differs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that, within 124M–774M, more parameters lower held-out native-text loss even when pretraining only on MT-derived data, with a Tamil Simplified-MT 774M exception. They report diminishing returns at 774M, tentatively due to the data-to-parameter ratio. They add that source-side simplification hurts transfer, and that MT pretraining plus native CPT often beats native-only pretraining. They call for broader scale and data variation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a parameter-size sweep and held-out cross-entropy, but tests MT-derived training corpora with native-text evaluation across three GPT-2 sizes; it does not fit power laws, extrapolate from small runs, or test tokens or compute scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Language and source-text condition differ; Tamil Simplified-MT has a slight worsening at 774M. The authors also report diminishing returns at 774M.
record.problems: Only three model sizes are tested, spanning 124M–774M; the study does not fit power laws or report exact loss values in the text for Figure 1. It uses fixed datasets and languages, and the authors say broader scale and data variation are needed.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant held-out-loss scaling conditions were left out. Downstream task and syntactic-probe outcomes were not extracted because they do not test the listed scaling-law claim versions as framed.

untested.parts: Power-law functional form; range over several orders of magnitude; scaling in tokens or compute; regimes where data is not the bottleneck (token budgets are fixed per condition).
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
MT-derived pretraining and continual pretraining are a transfer-like regime, but no power-law form is fitted in them.
No exponents or fits are compared.
No prediction from loss or scale is fitted; only raw accuracy across three sizes is available.

missing.what: Downstream fine-tuned balanced accuracy (SA, NLI, TD, CR) by model size for each pretraining condition, including non-monotonic cases and CR flat near chance
Zero-shot LINDSEA syntax accuracy by model size (e.g. Indonesian Native 53.6/52.4/57.4; Tamil Medium Simplified-MT-CPT 76.0 beats all Large models)
Authors' statement that language-modeling loss improvements (Natural vs Simplified) do not always translate into downstream gains

record.verdict_notes: Reader's 'downstream not relevant' gate is too strict: Tables 5, 6 and 9 report accuracy across sizes, which bears weakly on V6. All V1 support is directional only: three sizes, no fit, token budgets fixed, so the Large models may be data-limited. Neither original source is this study. The reader's T1 is changed to T3 (new MT-data setting, no power-law fit).

versions.untested_parts: Tests change in held-out loss with parameter count for 124M–774M GPT-2 models in the stated training settings. Does not fit or establish a power law, test several orders of magnitude, or sweep tokens or compute while holding the other quantities non-bottlenecked.
No small-run fits are used to predict larger-run losses.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token trend is tested.
No depth, width, or architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
The study uses text pretraining; it does not test the same power-law form across other modalities or the listed training regimes.
Downstream tasks are evaluated after fine-tuning, but the study does not test prediction of task performance from pretraining loss or scale.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits are compared across setups. The study notes diminishing returns and one loss exception, but does not fit or compare power-law curves.

rows.measure: Cross-entropy loss on held-out native text
rows.note: The authors state that loss decreases with larger MT-pretrained model size; exact curve values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: State holds only for the direction (loss falls with size). Power-law form cannot be read from three points spanning ~6x in parameters; values are figure-only.
